analysis.title: USA: Existing Home Sales Somewhat Below Expectations
key_insights: October existing home sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75mn SAAR, below the GS forecast of -4.0% (3.83mn) and the median forecast of -3.5% (3.85mn). It is the lowest level since July 2010.
GS says the weak print fits its expectation that higher mortgage rates will substantially depress housing turnover.

By type, sales fell 5.8% for single-family units and 2.9% for condos and co-ops. By region, sales fell 6.5% in the South, 3.2% in the Midwest and 9.7% in the West, and were unchanged in the Northeast.
The median sales price of all existing homes fell 0.3% month over month (SA by GS), a +0.4% year-over-year rate.
Months' supply of existing homes for sale rose to 4.7 months in October, the highest since February 2016 (SA by GS). GS says the supply-demand imbalance improved significantly.
GS expects the improved housing supply to make homebuilding more sensitive to higher mortgage rates.
GS lowered its Q4 GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +1.8% q/q annualized and left its Q3 tracking estimate unchanged at +3.5%.
